sentences.text: The holotype specimen indicates that this animal reached a length of 2 to 3 meters.

The internal bone structure of Nyasasaurus resembles that of the primitive dinosaur Coelophysis more than dinosaur ancestors, suggesting it was closer to dinosaur ancestry than other archosaurs of the time.
A 2012 analysis suggested Nyasasaurus could be the oldest known dinosaur, predating Herrerasaurus and Eoraptor by about 15 million years.
The holotype of Nyasasaurus was collected in the 1930s from the Lifua Member of the Manda Formation in southern Tanzania by Francis Rex Parrington.
Fossils of Nyasasaurus were collected in the 1930s by Francis Rex Parrington from the Parrington B36 locality in the Manda Formation near Lake Nyasa in southern Tanzania.
The remains were first described in 1956 in a doctoral thesis and referred to as Specimen 50b.
The remains were first described in a 1956 doctoral thesis by English paleontologist Alan J. Charig, who named the specimen "Specimen 50b".

A new description was published in 2013 by Sterling Nesbitt, Paul Barrett, Sarah Werning, and Christian Sidor, which ensured the validity of the name Nyasasaurus and changed the specific name to parringtoni in honor of Parrington.
A new description was published in 2012 by Sterling Nesbitt, Paul Barrett, Sarah Werning, and Christian Sidor, which included Charig as a posthumous co-author and validated the name.
Analysis of the humerus indicates rapid bone growth with interwoven fibers, many blood vessel channels, and few lines of arrested growth.
Affinities with dinosaurs have been tested based on a long deltopectoral crest on the humerus with a deviated upper part, a feature unequivocally present only in dinosaurs.
Nyasasaurus is considered a basal dinosaur or close to dinosaurs.
Nyasasaurus is confidently classified within Archosauria and Dinosauriformes, and possibly within Dinosauria.
Nyasasaurus is classified within the unranked order Dinosauromorpha.
Nyasasaurus is classified within the unranked family Dinosauriformes.
The humerus of Nyasasaurus does not share any unique traits exclusively with any other Triassic archosaur clade.
Nyasasaurus can be securely placed within Archosauria, Dinosauria, and possibly Dinosauriformes.

A 2017 phylogenetic analysis by Matthew Baron, David B. Norman, and Paul Barrett found that Nyasasaurus may represent a derived sauropodomorph more closely related to masospondylines like Massospondylus and Lufengosaurus.
The parent group of Nyasasaurus is listed as Dinosauria.
Nyasasaurus lived approximately 243 million years ago during the Anisian stage of the Middle Triassic in what is now Africa.
If radiometric dating is correct, Nyasasaurus would be Carnian in age, significantly reducing the time gap between it and other early dinosaurs.

A 2012 analysis suggests Nyasasaurus may be the oldest known dinosaur, dating to the Middle Triassic or late Anisian age, about 243 million years ago, 10 million years before other dinosaur species like Herrerasaurus.
A 1986 hypothesis suggested Nyasasaurus was a primitive prosauropod dinosaur, but this was disputed.
Not all paleontologists accept the younger Carnian age proposed for the formation containing Nyasasaurus.
The SHRIMP dating methods used to determine the age of the Río Seco de la Quebrada Formation have been criticized as less accurate than CA-TIMS dating.
It was suggested that Nyasasaurus was a primitive prosauropod dinosaur, but this hypothesis is questionable.
